questions.question: What is the frequency (f) of a wave with a period of 0.04 seconds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The frequency (f) of a wave is the reciprocal of its period (T).
 
• The formula to calculate frequency is f = 1/T.
 
• Given the period T = 0.04 seconds, applying the formula gives f = 1/0.04.
 
• Therefore, the frequency of the wave is f = 25 Hz.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frequency (f)**:

 
 
• Frequency is the number of complete wave cycles that pass a point per unit of time, typically measured in Hertz (Hz).
 
• 1 Hz is equal to one cycle per second.
 
 
 
• **Period (T)**:
 
 
• The period is the time taken for one complete cycle of the wave to pass a given point.
 
• It is usually measured in seconds (s).
 
 
 
• **Relationship between Period and Frequency**:
 
 
• The period is the inverse of the frequency: T = 1/f.
 
• Similarly, frequency is the inverse of the period: f = 1/T.
 
 
 
• **Wave Cycles**:
 
 
• A wave cycle consists of one complete wave oscillation, typically measured from crest to crest or trough to trough.

questions.question: International Day of Non-violence is observed on ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thu Oct 02 2025 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The International Day of Non-Violence is observed on **October 2nd** each year.
 
• This date was chosen to honor the birthday of **Mahatma Gandhi**, the leader of the Indian independence movement and a pioneer of the philosophy and strategy of non-violence.
 
• The day was established by the United Nations General Assembly in **2007**.
 
• The resolution for the International Day of Non-Violence was co-sponsored by **140 countries**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**:

 
 
• Born on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, India.
 
• Known for his principles of **Satyagraha** (truth and non-violence).
 
• Played a crucial role in India's struggle for independence from British rule.
 
• Assassinated on January 30, 1948, in New Delhi, India.
 
 
 
• **Non-Violence**:
 
 
• A philosophy and strategy for social change that rejects the use of violence.
 
• Prominent non-violent leaders include Martin Luther King Jr., Nelson Mandela, and Cesar Chavez.
 
• Non-violence is also a principle in various religious traditions, including Hinduism, Buddhism, and Christianity.
 
 
 
• **United Nations General Assembly**:
 
 
• One of the six principal organs of the United Nations.
 
• Comprises all 193 member states of the UN.
 
• Responsible for making important decisions on peace and security, admission of new members, and budgetary matters.
 
• Resolutions adopted by the General Assembly are non-binding but carry significant moral weight.
 
 
 
• **Global Observances**:
 
 
• International days are occasions to educate the public on issues of concern.
 
• They mobilize political will and resources to address global problems.
 
• Examples include International Women's Day (March 8), World Health Day (April 7), and International Day of Peace (September 21).

questions.question: Which of the following wars took place in the year 1761?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panipat III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Third Battle of Panipat was fought on **January 14, 1761**, between the Maratha Empire and the Durrani Empire (Afghan forces led by Ahmad Shah Abdali).
 
• This battle is considered one of the largest and bloodiest fought in the 18th century, involving over 125,000 soldiers.
 
• The Marathas were led by their commander-in-chief, **Sadashivrao Bhau**, while the Afghan forces were commanded by Ahmad Shah Abdali.
 
• The battle resulted in a decisive victory for the Durrani Empire, marking the end of Maratha expansion in North India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Causes of the Battle:**

 
 
• The Marathas aimed to expand their influence in Northern India, which led to conflicts with regional powers including the Durrani Empire.
 
• The battle was also a result of the declining Mughal Empire, which left a power vacuum in the region.
 
 
 
• **Key Figures:**
 
 
• Ahmad Shah Abdali, also known as Ahmad Shah Durrani, was the founder of the Durrani Empire and one of the most successful military leaders of his time.
 
• Sadashivrao Bhau, the Maratha commander-in-chief, was the nephew of the Peshwa and a capable military leader.
 
 
 
• **Consequences:**
 
 
• The defeat at Panipat weakened the Maratha Empire significantly, leading to internal strife and a temporary setback in their quest for dominance.
 
• The battle also paved the way for the eventual rise of British power in India as the Marathas were one of the main obstacles to their expansion.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The Third Battle of Panipat is remembered for its high casualties and the significant impact it had on the Indian subcontinent's political landscape.
 
• It is often studied as a key example of the complex interplay of regional powers during the 18th century in India.

questions.question: The Sarda River rises in the ________ glacier in the Nepal Himalayas.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Milam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sarda River originates from the **Milam Glacier** in the Nepal Himalayas.
 
• Milam Glacier is located in the **Pithoragarh district of Uttarakhand, India**.
 
• The glacier is about **16 km long** and lies at an altitude of approximately **3,870 meters above sea level**.
 
• The Sarda River, also known as **Kali or Mahakali River**, forms a part of the India-Nepal border.
 
• The river eventually joins the Ghaghara River, a major left-bank tributary of the Ganges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayan Glaciers:**

 
 
• Glaciers in the Himalayas are crucial sources of freshwater for rivers in the region.
 
• They play a vital role in sustaining the hydrology and ecology of the surrounding areas.
 
 
 
• **Hydrological Importance:**
 
 
• The Sarda River is an important water source for irrigation and hydroelectricity in both India and Nepal.
 
• It supports agriculture and provides drinking water to millions of people.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Significance:**
 
 
• The Sarda River forms a natural border between India and Nepal, and there are various treaties and agreements regarding its use.
 
• Both countries collaborate on issues related to water sharing and flood management.
 
 
 
• **Milam Glacier Trek:**
 
 
• The Milam Glacier is a popular trekking destination, attracting adventure enthusiasts from around the world.
 
• The trek offers stunning views of the Himalayan landscape and a chance to explore remote villages.

questions.question: Which of the following iron and steel plants is located in Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rourkela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rourkela Steel Plant (RSP) is located in Rourkela, Odisha, and was the first integrated steel plant in the public sector in India.
 
• It was set up with the collaboration of Germany and started production in 1959.
 
• RSP is operated by the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), which is one of the largest state-owned steel-making companies in India.
 
• The plant is known for producing a wide variety of steel products, including hot-rolled coils, plates, and pipes.
 
• Rourkela is strategically located in the mineral-rich state of Odisha, making it ideal for steel production due to the availability of raw materials like iron ore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijay Nagar**:

 
 
• Vijay Nagar is home to the Vijayanagar Steel Plant, which is operated by JSW Steel in Karnataka.
 
• It is one of the largest steel plants in India with a production capacity of over 12 million tonnes per year.
 
 
 
• **Bokaro**:
 
 
• Bokaro Steel Plant is located in Bokaro, Jharkhand, and is operated by SAIL.
 
• It is known for producing flat products like hot-rolled and cold-rolled coils and sheets.
 
 
 
• **Vishakhapatnam**:
 
 
• Vishakhapatnam Steel Plant, also known as Vizag Steel, is located in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is operated by Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), a public sector enterprise.
 
 
 
• **Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)**:
 
 
• SAIL is one of the largest state-owned steel-making companies in India and operates multiple integrated steel plants across the country.
 
• It was established in 1954 and is headquartered in New Delhi.

questions.question:
What is the product of the following chemical reaction?

NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Baking soda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Baking soda is chemically known as **sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3)**.
 
• The reaction of NaCl, H2O, CO2, and NH3 produces baking soda as one of the products.
 
• This reaction is part of the **Solvay process**, an industrial method for producing sodium carbonate (Na2CO3).
 
• Baking soda is used in various applications including cooking, cleaning, and as an antacid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solvay Process:**

 
 
• Developed by Ernest Solvay in 1861.
 
• It is an industrial method for the production of sodium carbonate (washing soda).
 
• Involves the reaction of sodium chloride, ammonia, and carbon dioxide in water.
 
• The process is more environmentally friendly compared to the older Leblanc process.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sodium Bicarbonate:**
 
 
• Used in baking as a leavening agent.
 
• Commonly used as an antacid to treat heartburn and indigestion.
 
• Utilized in fire extinguishers for chemical and electrical fires.
 
• Employed in cleaning products due to its mild abrasive properties.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Properties of Sodium Bicarbonate:**
 
 
• It is a white crystalline solid or a fine powder.
 
• Soluble in water, producing a mildly alkaline solution.
 
• When heated, it decomposes to produce sodium carbonate, water, and carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• The Solvay process is less polluting than the Leblanc process, producing fewer byproducts.
 
• Baking soda itself is non-toxic and environmentally benign.

questions.question: Minor points called 'Yuko' are part of which of the following sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Yuko** is a scoring term used in **Judo** competitions.
 
• It was part of the traditional judo scoring system but was removed in 2017 to simplify the scoring.
 
• Yuko was awarded for techniques that were not as dominant as Ippon or Waza-ari but still demonstrated control and skill.
 
• In modern Judo, the remaining scores are Ippon and Waza-ari, with Ippon being the highest score leading to an immediate win.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judo**:

 
 
• A modern martial art, combat, and Olympic sport created in Japan by Kano Jigoro in 1882.
 
• The objective is to either throw or takedown an opponent, immobilize, or otherwise subdue them with a pin, or force an opponent to submit with a joint lock or a choke.
 
 
 
• **Ippon**:
 
 
• The highest score in Judo, awarded for a throw that places the opponent on their back with considerable force and speed or for a submission.
 
 
 
• **Waza-ari**:
 
 
• A score awarded for a throw that is not quite an Ippon but still effective, or for controlling the opponent on the ground for a certain period.
 
 
 
• **Golden Score**:
 
 
• In case of a tie at the end of the match, the Golden Score rule is applied, where the first player to score wins.

questions.question: At which sports event in India is the Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy awarded?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Games of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy is awarded during the **National Games of India**.
 
• This trophy is awarded to the state or union territory with the best overall performance in the National Games.
 
• The National Games of India is a multi-sport event held at intervals, where athletes from across the country compete.
 
• The trophy is named in honor of Raja Bhalindra Singh, who was a notable sports administrator and the president of the Indian Olympic Association.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Games of India:**

 
 
• The National Games are organized by the Indian Olympic Association.
 
• The first edition of the National Games was held in 1924 in Lahore.
 
• It aims to identify and nurture talent for international competitions like the Asian Games and the Olympics.
 
 
 
• **Raja Bhalindra Singh:**
 
 
• Raja Bhalindra Singh was a member of the Patiala royal family.
 
• He played a significant role in promoting sports in India.
 
• He also served as the President of the Indian Olympic Association from 1960 to 1975.
 
 
 
• **Indian Olympic Association (IOA):**
 
 
• The IOA is responsible for the selection and management of athletes representing India in the Olympic Games.
 
• It was established in 1927 and is affiliated with the International Olympic Committee.
 
 
 
• **Multi-Sport Events:**
 
 
• Multi-sport events like the National Games help in the comprehensive development of athletes across various sports.
 
• They provide a platform for athletes to compete at a high level and gain valuable experience.

questions.question: Which great Indian classical dancer choreographed the songs for Madhuri Dixit in 'Devdas' and 'Dil To Pagal Hai' movies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Birju Maharaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Birju Maharaj** is one of the most celebrated Indian classical dancers, known for his expertise in Kathak dance.
 
• He choreographed the song "Kahe Chhed Mohe" for Madhuri Dixit in the film **'Devdas'** (2002).
 
• He also choreographed the Kathak sequences for the song "Kaahe Chhed" in the film **'Dil To Pagal Hai'** (1997), performed by Madhuri Dixit.
 
• Birju Maharaj has received numerous awards, including the **Padma Vibhushan**, India's second-highest civilian award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak Dance:**

 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• It is traditionally attributed to the traveling bards of ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• The dance form emphasizes intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures.
 
 
 
• **Devdas (2002):**
 
 
• Directed by Sanjay Leela Bhansali, the film is based on the 1917 novel of the same name by Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay.
 
• Madhuri Dixit played the role of Chandramukhi, a courtesan.
 
• The film is known for its elaborate set designs and classical dance performances.
 
 
 
• **Dil To Pagal Hai (1997):**
 
 
• Directed by Yash Chopra, the film is a musical romantic drama.
 
• Madhuri Dixit played the role of Pooja, a dancer and choreographer.
 
• The film was notable for its contemporary dance sequences.
 
 
 
• **Padma Vibhushan:**
 
 
• It is the second-highest civilian award in India after the Bharat Ratna.
 
• It is awarded for exceptional and distinguished service in any field including government service.
 
• Birju Maharaj received this honor in 1986 for his contributions to Indian classical dance.

questions.question: Which famous medieval singer was born in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh in the year 1506?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tansen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tansen**, also known as Ramtanu, was born in 1506 in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.
 
• He was one of the **Navaratnas** (nine gems) at the court of Emperor Akbar.
 
• Tansen is often regarded as the **greatest musician** in Indian classical music.
 
• He was a disciple of **Swami Haridas** and later became a prominent figure in the court of Akbar.
 
• Tansen is known for his contributions to **Hindustani classical music**, including the creation of several ragas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Navaratnas:**

 
 
• Refers to the nine extraordinary talents in Emperor Akbar's court.
 
• Included notable figures such as Birbal, Raja Todar Mal, and Abul Fazl.
 
 
 
• **Swami Haridas:**
 
 
• A renowned musician and spiritual figure of the Bhakti movement.
 
• Guru of Tansen and believed to be an avatar of Lalita, a companion of Krishna.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani Classical Music:**
 
 
• A genre of Indian classical music from North India.
 
• Involves complex ragas and talas, forming the melodic and rhythmic structure.
 
 
 
• **Ragas:**
 
 
• Frameworks for musical improvisation and composition in Indian classical music.
 
• Each raga has its own distinctive mood and set of rules.

questions.question: If a citizen is helping the government in protecting the monuments in his/her area, which of the following fundamental duties is he/she performing?

options.text: Valuing and preserving the rich heritage and culture

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Valuing and preserving the rich heritage and culture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Valuing and preserving the rich heritage and culture is one of the fundamental duties listed in Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This duty emphasizes the importance of protecting and conserving the cultural heritage of India.
 
• It includes the responsibility of every citizen to safeguard the monuments, places, and objects of artistic or historic interest.
 
• This duty aims to promote a sense of pride among citizens for the rich cultural legacy of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties are enshrined in Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties are intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens of their responsibilities towards the nation.
 
• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• There are 11 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A.
 
 
 
• **Protection of Monuments:**
 
 
• The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) is responsible for the preservation of ancient monuments and archaeological sites.
 
• There are laws such as the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958, that protect these sites.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Heritage:**
 
 
• India is home to 40 UNESCO World Heritage Sites as of 2023.
 
• The cultural heritage includes monuments, traditions, languages, and art forms passed down through generations.
 
 
 
• **Citizens' Role:**
 
 
• Citizens can participate in heritage walks, awareness campaigns, and volunteer for organizations dedicated to heritage conservation.
 
• Reporting vandalism or illegal activities around heritage sites to authorities is also a way to contribute to preservation.

questions.question: In which year was the first-ever motion to remove a Supreme Court Justice signed by the members of Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1991**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first-ever motion to remove a Supreme Court Justice in India was signed in **1991**.
 
• The motion was targeted at Justice V. Ramaswami, who faced allegations of financial irregularities.
 
• The motion was initiated by the then Law Minister Subramanian Swamy.
 
• The process led to the formation of a three-member judicial committee to investigate the charges.
 
• Although the committee found him guilty, the motion did not pass in the Lok Sabha due to lack of requisite majority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Impeachment Process of Judges**

 
 
• The procedure for the removal of judges is outlined in Article 124(4) and Article 217 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• A judge can be removed on grounds of proven misbehavior or incapacity.
 
• The process can be initiated in either House of Parliament.
 
• The motion needs to be supported by a specified number of members before it can be admitted.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Committee**
 
 
• Once the motion is admitted, a three-member committee investigates the charges.
 
• The committee consists of a Supreme Court judge, a Chief Justice of a High Court, and a distinguished jurist.
 
 
 
• **Final Decision**
 
 
• If the committee finds the judge guilty, the House can take up the motion for debate and voting.
 
• The motion must be passed by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting in each House of Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• Justice V. Ramaswami was the first Supreme Court judge to face an impeachment motion.
 
• The case highlighted the need for transparency and accountability in the judiciary.

questions.question: Which of the following communicable diseases is caused by bacteria?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cholera**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cholera** is an acute diarrheal infection caused by ingestion of food or water contaminated with the bacterium *Vibrio cholerae*.
 
• It can cause severe dehydration and, if untreated, can lead to death within hours.
 
• Cholera outbreaks are often linked to inadequate access to clean water and sanitation facilities.
 
• The disease is most common in places with poor sanitation, crowding, war, and famine.
 
• Cholera can be prevented with proper sanitation, clean drinking water, and oral cholera vaccines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vibrio cholerae:** The bacterium responsible for cholera, which produces a toxin that causes the rapid loss of fluids and electrolytes.
 
• **Symptoms:** Include severe watery diarrhea, vomiting, and leg cramps. In severe cases, it can lead to shock and death within hours.
 
• **Transmission:** Mainly occurs through the consumption of contaminated water or food. Person-to-person transmission is rare.
 
• **Prevention:** Access to safe drinking water, improved sanitation, and hygiene practices are critical to preventing cholera.
 
• **Treatment:** Prompt rehydration with oral rehydration salts (ORS) or intravenous fluids, and antibiotics in severe cases, are effective treatments for cholera.

questions.question: Suspended solids in water can increase the haziness of the water. Which of the following represents the measurement of haziness of water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Turbidity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Turbidity** is the measure of the degree to which water loses its transparency due to the presence of suspended particulates.
 
• It is an important indicator of water quality and clarity, with higher turbidity indicating higher levels of suspended solids.
 
• Turbidity is commonly measured in Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU).
 
• High turbidity can indicate potential contamination and can affect aquatic life by reducing the amount of light penetrating the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solubility:**

 
 
• Solubility refers to the ability of a substance to dissolve in a solvent, forming a homogeneous solution at a specified temperature and pressure.
 
• It is typically expressed in terms of the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent.
 
 
 
• **Salinity:**
 
 
• Salinity is the measure of all the salts dissolved in water, usually expressed in parts per thousand (ppt).
 
• It is an important factor in determining the chemical and physical properties of water.
 
 
 
• **Viscosity:**
 
 
• Viscosity is the measure of a fluid's resistance to flow or deformation.
 
• It is an intrinsic property of the fluid and is influenced by temperature and pressure.

questions.question: In June 2023, who was appointed as the new Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chief?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravi Sinha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ravi Sinha was appointed as the new chief of the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) in June 2023.
 
• He succeeded Samant Goel, the previous head of RAW.
 
• Ravi Sinha is a 1988-batch officer of the Indian Police Service (IPS).
 
• Prior to his appointment, he was serving as the Special Secretary in the Cabinet Secretariat.
 
• His appointment was approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), headed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Research and Analysis Wing (RAW):**

 
 
• RAW is India's primary foreign intelligence agency.
 
• It was established in September 1968 following the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965.
 
• The agency's primary function is to gather intelligence related to foreign threats to India's national security.
 
• RAW operates under the aegis of the Cabinet Secretariat.
 
 
 
• **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC):**
 
 
• The ACC is responsible for appointments to several top posts under the Government of India.
 
• It is composed of the Prime Minister and the Minister of Home Affairs.
 
• The ACC has the authority to approve appointments to various key positions including heads of central intelligence agencies.
 
 
 
• **Indian Police Service (IPS):**
 
 
• IPS is one of the three All India Services of the Government of India.
 
• Officers of the IPS provide senior-level leadership to police forces both at the Centre and in states.
 
• They are recruited through the Civil Services Examination conducted by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).
 
 
 
• **Cabinet Secretariat:**
 
 
• The Cabinet Secretariat is responsible for the administration of the Government of India.
 
• It functions directly under the Prime Minister and coordinates between various ministries and departments of the government.
 
• The Secretary to the Cabinet is the administrative head of the Secretariat.

questions.question: In 1917, Mahatma Gandhi started his first satyagraha in India against the forced cultivation of indigo by Europeans in which of the following districts of British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first satyagraha led by Mahatma Gandhi in India was held in **Champaran** district of Bihar in 1917.
 
• It was a significant movement against the **forced cultivation of indigo** by European planters.
 
• Gandhi's involvement was sparked by the plight of the farmers who were compelled to grow indigo on a portion of their land and sell it at prices fixed by the British planters.
 
• Gandhi's successful intervention in Champaran marked the beginning of the mass civil disobedience movement in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satyagraha**:

 
 
• A method of nonviolent resistance or civil resistance developed by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The term means "truth force" or "soul force".
 
• It played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement and influenced movements for civil rights and freedom across the world.
 
 
 
• **Indigo Cultivation**:
 
 
• Indigo was a significant cash crop during the British rule in India.
 
• Farmers were forced to grow indigo on a part of their land, often to the detriment of their food crops.
 
• The exploitation and harsh conditions led to widespread resentment and resistance among the farmers.
 
 
 
• **Champaran Movement Impact**:
 
 
• Highlighted the plight of farmers under colonial rule.
 
• Led to the abolition of the Tinkathia system, which compelled farmers to grow indigo.
 
• Marked a significant milestone in the Indian struggle for independence.
 
 
 
• **Role of Local Leaders**:
 
 
• Local leaders like Raj Kumar Shukla played a vital role in bringing Gandhi to Champaran.
 
• The movement also saw the involvement of other prominent leaders like Rajendra Prasad and Anugrah Narayan Sinha.

questions.question: After the ________ of Hakim Mirza, Kabul was annexed by Akbar and given to Raja Man Singh as ‘jagir’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**death**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hakim Mirza, also known as Mirza Muhammad Hakim, was the ruler of Kabul and a half-brother of Mughal Emperor Akbar.
 
• After his death in 1585, Akbar annexed Kabul into the Mughal Empire.
 
• Kabul was subsequently given to Raja Man Singh as a 'jagir' by Akbar.
 
• This consolidation helped Akbar strengthen his control over the north-western frontier of his empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Akbar the Great:**

 
 
• Akbar, the third Mughal Emperor, reigned from 1556 to 1605.
 
• He is known for his military conquests, administrative innovations, and efforts to foster religious tolerance.
 
• Akbar's reign significantly expanded the Mughal Empire and is often referred to as a golden age in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Raja Man Singh:**
 
 
• Raja Man Singh was a prominent general in Akbar’s court and one of his Navaratnas (nine gems).
 
• He played a crucial role in several military campaigns, including those in Bengal, Bihar, and Kabul.
 
 
 
• **Kabul:**
 
 
• Kabul was an important strategic location for the Mughal Empire, serving as a gateway to Central Asia.
 
• The region was known for its economic and cultural significance during the Mughal period.
 
 
 
• **Jagir:**
 
 
• A 'jagir' was a type of land grant given by the Mughal Emperor to his nobles and officials in lieu of a salary.
 
• The holder of a jagir, known as a jagirdar, was responsible for the administration and revenue collection of the area.

questions.question: In January 2024, Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tributes to Savitribai Phule on her birth anniversary. In which field did Savitribai Phule make significant contributions, as highlighted by Prime Minister Modi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Education and social reform**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Savitribai Phule is recognized as one of the first female teachers in India.
 
• She, along with her husband Jyotirao Phule, played a pivotal role in promoting women's education.
 
• She was a social reformer who worked tirelessly for the upliftment of women and the lower castes in 19th century India.
 
• Savitribai Phule established several schools for girls in Maharashtra and was a pioneer in the field of education.
 
• Her efforts also included fighting against social evils such as child marriage and the caste system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Women's Education in India:**

 
 
• Women's education in India has been a major concern since the early 19th century, with social reformers like Savitribai Phule playing a crucial role.
 
• Access to education for women has significantly improved, but disparities still exist, particularly in rural areas.
 
• Government schemes like Beti Bachao Beti Padhao aim to promote gender equality and improve women's education.
 
 
 
• **Social Reform Movements:**
 
 
• Social reform movements in India have aimed to eradicate social evils and promote equality and justice.
 
• Key figures include Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Jyotirao Phule.
 
• These movements addressed issues like sati, child marriage, untouchability, and women's rights.
 
 
 
• **Jyotirao Phule:**
 
 
• Jyotirao Phule was an Indian social activist, thinker, and writer.
 
• He, along with his wife Savitribai, founded the first Indian girl’s school in Pune in 1848.
 
• Phule was a strong advocate for the education of women and lower caste members.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Education on Social Reform:**
 
 
• Education has been a key tool in driving social reform and improving the socio-economic status of marginalized communities.
 
• Educated individuals are better equipped to challenge societal norms and advocate for their rights.
 
• Education fosters critical thinking and promotes values of equality, justice, and democracy.

questions.question: For which English novel was Ruskin Bond honoured with the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992?

options.text: Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ruskin Bond was honoured with the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992 for his English novel **"Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra".**
 
• The award recognizes and promotes excellence in Indian literature.
 
• **"Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra"** is a collection of short stories that reflect Bond's attachment to Dehradun and his life experiences.
 
• The book is a blend of nostalgia and the author's observations of the changing landscapes and people in Dehra.
 
• Ruskin Bond is renowned for his simple and poignant writing style that captures the essence of rural India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award**:

 
 
• The Sahitya Akademi Award is a literary honour in India, presented annually by the Sahitya Akademi, India's National Academy of Letters.
 
• It recognizes outstanding works of literature in the 24 major Indian languages, including English.
 
• The award includes a plaque and a cash prize.
 
• It is one of the most prestigious literary awards in India, aimed at promoting and preserving Indian literature.
 
 
 
• **Ruskin Bond**:
 
 
• Ruskin Bond is an acclaimed Indian author of British descent, known for his vivid portrayal of life in the Indian hill stations.
 
• He has written numerous novels, short stories, essays, and children's books.
 
• Bond has received several awards for his contribution to literature, including the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.
 
• His works often reflect his deep connection with nature and the simplicity of rural life.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Works by Ruskin Bond**:
 
 
• "The Room on the Roof" – His first novel, which won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize in 1957.
 
• "The Blue Umbrella" – A beloved children's story that was adapted into a film.
 
• "A Flight of Pigeons" – A novella that was adapted into the film "Junoon".
 
• "Delhi Is Not Far" – A novel that showcases the author's talent for storytelling.

questions.question: Who was the successor of Vima Kadphises in Kushana dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanishka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kanishka** was the successor of **Vima Kadphises** and is one of the most notable rulers of the Kushana dynasty.
 
• Kanishka's reign is generally believed to have begun around **78 AD**, which also marks the start of the Saka Era.
 
• He is renowned for his military, spiritual, and cultural achievements, significantly expanding the Kushana Empire.
 
• Kanishka is also known for his patronage of Buddhism and convening the **Fourth Buddhist Council** in Kashmir.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kushana Dynasty**

 
 
• The Kushana dynasty ruled over regions in Central Asia and the northern Indian subcontinent from approximately 1st to 3rd centuries AD.
 
• The dynasty is known for its contributions to the cultural and artistic heritage of the region, including the spread of Gandhara art.
 
• Key rulers include Kujula Kadphises, Vima Kadphises, and Kanishka.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Buddhist Council**
 
 
• Held under the patronage of Kanishka in Kashmir around 1st century AD.
 
• This council led to the compilation of significant Buddhist texts and the spread of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Saka Era**
 
 
• The Saka Era began in 78 AD during the reign of Kanishka.
 
• It is one of the historical Indian calendars still in use in some contexts today.
 
 
 
• **Gandhara Art**
 
 
• A style of Buddhist visual art that developed in what is now northwestern Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan between the 1st and 7th centuries AD.
 
• Gandhara art is known for its syncretic style combining Indian, Greek, and Persian influences.

questions.question: In which region of Bangladesh do the Chakma people predominantly live, among the country's various indigenous ethnic groups?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittagong Hill Tracts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Chakma people predominantly reside in the **Chittagong Hill Tracts** region of Bangladesh.
 
• The Chittagong Hill Tracts is located in the southeastern part of Bangladesh and is known for its hilly terrain and dense forests.
 
• Alongside the Chakmas, other indigenous groups such as the Marma and Tripura also inhabit this region.
 
• The Chakmas are the largest ethnic group in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, and their culture and traditions are distinct from the majority Bengali population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chittagong Hill Tracts**

 
 
• The Chittagong Hill Tracts is divided into three districts: Bandarban, Rangamati, and Khagrachari.
 
• It covers an area of approximately 13,295 square kilometers, making it a significant region in terms of both geography and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Chakma People**
 
 
• The Chakmas practice Theravada Buddhism, which is a major part of their cultural identity.
 
• They have their own language, Chakma, which belongs to the Indo-Aryan language family.
 
 
 
• **Indigenous Rights**
 
 
• The Chittagong Hill Tracts Peace Accord was signed in 1997, aimed at resolving long-standing conflicts between the government and indigenous groups.
 
• The Accord granted the indigenous communities certain administrative and cultural autonomy.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Significance**
 
 
• The region shares borders with India and Myanmar, making it strategically important.
 
• Issues related to land rights, migration, and integration of indigenous people remain significant challenges in the area.

questions.question: Which Ministry of India launched the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY)?

options.text: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Labour & Employment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) was launched by the **Ministry of Labour & Employment**.
 
• This scheme aims to incentivize employers for generating new employment opportunities.
 
• Under PMRPY, the Government of India pays the full employer’s contribution towards the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) and Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) for new employees for a period of three years.
 
• The scheme is targeted towards workers earning wages up to ₹15,000 per month.
 
• PMRPY was launched to accelerate employment generation in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Employees' Provident Fund (EPF)**:

 
 
• EPF is a retirement benefit scheme for salaried employees managed by the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).
 
• Both employer and employee contribute 12% of the employee’s basic salary towards EPF.
 
 
 
• **Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS)**:
 
 
• EPS is a pension scheme managed by the EPFO, providing pension benefits to employees after retirement.
 
• The employer’s contribution towards EPS is 8.33% of the employee’s basic salary, subject to a maximum of ₹1,250 per month.
 
 
 
• **Unorganized Sector**:
 
 
• The unorganized sector comprises workers who are not employed in fixed, formal jobs or are not covered by any social security measures.
 
• Examples include casual laborers, small-scale farmers, and self-employed individuals.
 
 
 
• **Social Security Schemes in India**:
 
 
• Social security schemes in India are designed to provide financial support and security to individuals in the event of retirement, disability, or other contingencies.
 
• Examples include the Atal Pension Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan, and the National Pension System.

questions.question: Who received the National Nritya Shiromani award 2019 for promoting Kathak dance form across the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anindita Neogy Anaam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anindita Neogy Anaam is a renowned Kathak dancer known for her remarkable contributions to the dance form.
 
• She received the National Nritya Shiromani award in 2019 for promoting Kathak across the globe.
 
• The award was presented at the 10th Cuttack Mahotsav: International Dance and Music Festival held in Odisha.
 
• Anindita is celebrated for her innovative approach in blending traditional Kathak with contemporary elements, making it more appealing to the younger generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak Dance Form:**

 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating from Northern India.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures.
 
• The dance form traditionally narrates stories from Indian epics, folklore, and mythology.
 
• Kathak has three main gharanas (schools) - Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras, each with its unique style and emphasis.
 
 
 
• **National Nritya Shiromani Award:**
 
 
• This award is given to exceptional dancers who have significantly contributed to the promotion and preservation of Indian classical dance forms.
 
• It recognizes artists who have achieved excellence in their field and have promoted the art form both nationally and internationally.
 
 
 
• **Cuttack Mahotsav:**
 
 
• An international festival that celebrates dance and music, held annually in Cuttack, Odisha.
 
• The festival aims to promote cultural exchange and provides a platform for artists from various parts of the world to showcase their talents.
 
 
 
• **Role of Dance Festivals:**
 
 
• Dance festivals play a crucial role in preserving and promoting cultural heritage.
 
• They provide a platform for emerging artists to perform and gain recognition.
 
• Such festivals encourage the younger generation to appreciate and learn classical dance forms.

questions.question: Which Indian dynasty is associated with the creation of highly skilled bronze sculptures?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chola**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chola dynasty is renowned for its exceptional craftsmanship in creating bronze sculptures, particularly during the 9th to 13th centuries.
 
• Chola bronze sculptures are characterized by their intricate details and lifelike representation of deities, especially those of Shiva, Parvati, and Nataraja.
 
• The lost-wax casting technique, also known as "cire perdue," was predominantly used by Chola artisans to achieve high precision in their sculptures.
 
• The most iconic representation of Chola bronze art is the Nataraja, depicting Lord Shiva in his cosmic dance form, which symbolizes the cycle of creation and destruction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lost-Wax Casting Technique**:

 
 
• An ancient method of metal casting where a molten metal is poured into a mold created from a wax model.
 
• The wax model is melted and drained away, leaving a hollow form that is filled with molten metal to create the sculpture.
 
 
 
• **Nataraja**:
 
 
• A depiction of the Hindu god Shiva as the cosmic dancer who performs his divine dance to destroy a weary universe and make preparations for the god Brahma to start the process of creation.
 
• The Nataraja iconography is highly symbolic, with the dance representing the rhythmic movement of the universe.
 
 
 
• **Patronage of Arts**:
 
 
• The Chola dynasty was known for its patronage of arts, including temple architecture, painting, and sculpture.
 
• Under their rule, many grand temples were constructed, which served as hubs for artistic activity.
 
 
 
• **Chola Temples**:
 
 
• Notable for their grandeur and intricate architectural designs.
 
• The Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur is one of the most famous examples of Chola architecture.

questions.question: What is Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the context of National Income Accounting?

options.text: The total exports of a country
The total savings of a nation
The total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific period
The total income of a country's government

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific period**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) represents the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country during a specific period, usually a year or a quarter.
 
• It is a key indicator used to gauge the health of a country's economy and overall economic activity.
 
• GDP can be measured using three approaches: production (or output) approach, income approach, and expenditure approach.
 
• Real GDP is adjusted for inflation, providing a more accurate reflection of an economy's size and how it is growing over time.
 
• The growth rate of GDP is used to compare the economic performance of different countries or regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross National Product (GNP):**

 
 
• GNP measures the total economic output produced by a country's residents, regardless of the location of the production.
 
• It includes GDP plus income earned by residents from overseas investments minus income earned within the domestic economy by foreign residents.
 
 
 
• **Net National Product (NNP):**
 
 
• NNP is derived by subtracting depreciation (the loss of value of capital goods over time) from GNP.
 
• It represents the net value of goods and services produced by a country's residents.
 
 
 
• **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP):**
 
 
• PPP is an economic theory that compares different countries' currencies through a "basket of goods" approach.
 
• It is used to determine the relative value of currencies and to compare the cost of living between different countries.
 
 
 
• **Per Capita GDP:**
 
 
• Per Capita GDP is the average economic output per person, calculated by dividing the GDP by the total population.
 
• It is often used as an indicator of the standard of living and economic well-being of a country's residents.
